widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE - Turns pictures into the model's own format and back. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can hand back a transparent picture.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load Image - The picture to change. The result is this picture, full size, with only the painted area changed.
  • 2. Inpaint Crop - paint the mask - Open its mask editor with the button on the node, paint over what you want to change, and press Save. It cuts a working area around your mask and hands it to the model at about 1024 pixels, so even a small area gets full detail.
  • 3. Add a prompt - What to change in the painted area.
  • 4. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same result, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The speed nodes

Teal, above the graph.

  • Qwen Image 2.1 Cache - Where the model keeps what it has already worked out about your pictures and the prompt, so it does not redo that on every step. Leave it on auto / default. The note in 2 (One Image Edit) says when to change it.
  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The helper

Purple. It runs by itself.

  • Split Image with Alpha - Qwen Image 2.1 hands back every picture with a transparency channel. This drops it, so Inpaint Stitch pastes clean colours on any Pixaroma version.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads your prompt and the working area, resized to about 1024 x 1024 first. It also makes the blank canvas for the result, at the shape of the working area. Its negative prompt box does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • KSampler - The render: 25 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1, the settings from ComfyUI's own template.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.
  • Inpaint Stitch Pixaroma - Puts the changed area back into your full picture and softens the edge of the mask, so no seam shows. Everything outside the mask stays exactly as it was.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Image Compare Pixaroma - Your original picture and the result, one over the other. Move the mouse across it to slide between them.
  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the result and saves it to your output folder as a PNG.

The dark Run Timer above them shows how long the last Run took.

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

Your picture with one area changed, following your prompt: here, the green tie becomes a red one. Everything outside the area you paint stays exactly as it was.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 How long a Run takes

What changedTime
New mask or prompt8 s
New seed only7 s

Only the working area around your mask is rendered, at about 1024 pixels, so the time barely depends on how big your picture is.

The graphics card peaked at about 19 GB during these runs.

 Painting the mask

  • Click the button on Inpaint Crop to open the editor. Paint with the brush, erase with the eraser, then press Save.
  • The workflow opens with no mask painted, so paint one before the first Run. With no mask, the whole picture is the working area and it behaves like a normal edit.
  • Softness on Inpaint Crop is how far the edge of the mask fades into the picture. Inpaint Stitch has its own softness too, which overrides it without running the model again.

 Writing the prompt

  • Describe only the change, and add Keep everything else exactly as it is.
  • Paint a little wider than the thing you are changing, so the new one has room.
  • The mask is not handed to the model as a picture. Tested: the model then painted the white mask shape into the photo. The crop and the stitch alone keep the change inside the mask.

Tested on the tie on 8 seeds, and on earlier pictures on 13 more: every result was clean, with no seam, and nothing outside the painted area changed.

 The other edit workflows

Kitchen attention, the memory node, the first Run of the session and the full size table are explained in 2 (One Image Edit). They work the same way here.
